key_insight: A single, learned semantic–geometric task-graph representation can jointly capture discrete task structure and the time-varying, object-centric geometric relations from human demonstrations, enabling reasoning about long-horizon, bimanual manipulation.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of representing and reasoning about both the semantic ordering of actions and the evolving spatial relationships between objects in variable bimanual demonstrations so robots can understand and predict task progression.
method: Extract object-centric trajectories and semantic event labels from human bimanual demonstrations to form the basic elements of a task graph.

Build a joint semantic–geometric graph where nodes encode task semantics (steps/objects) and edges encode temporally evolving geometric relations; learn this representation with a graph-based model (e.g., graph neural components) from demonstrations.
Use temporal modeling over the graph to track task progression and enable prediction, generalization, and downstream planning or imitation.
impact: Provides a compact, interpretable representation that improves a robot’s ability to generalize and plan across long-horizon, multi-object bimanual tasks from human demos—useful for imitation learning, task inference, and structured planning in robotics research and applications.
visual_elements: Schematic of a semantic–geometric task graph: nodes (semantic steps/objects) with colored edges showing geometric relations (distances/orientations) that change over time.
Timeline or sequence strip showing object-centric frames from a bimanual demonstration with evolving relation overlays (e.g., relative pose arrows).
Diagram comparing raw demonstrations → learned graph representation → downstream uses (prediction, planning, imitation).
Bar/line chart summarizing gains: generalization to new object configurations and success rate for long-horizon tasks.
paper_title: Learning Semantic-Geometric Task Graph-Representations from Human Demonstrations
paper_authors: Franziska Herbert, Vignesh Prasad, Han Liu, Dorothea Koert, Georgia Chalvatzaki
